title: Senior's toolkit: the local network
summary: Links, neighbours, ARP, VLAN interfaces and DHCP: the commands that show what is happening on the LAN segment you are plugged into.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: the local network
steps.body: When a host cannot reach its own gateway, the problem is on the local segment: the link, ARP, the VLAN or DHCP. These commands look at each in turn.

toolkit.what: Each interface with UP or DOWN and its MAC address. A `NO-CARRIER` or `DOWN` here ends the search before it starts.
flags: packet, error and drop counters for one interface

toolkit.what: The ARP (IPv4) and neighbour (IPv6) cache: which MAC each local IP maps to, and whether it is `REACHABLE`, `STALE` or `FAILED`.
flags: ARP got no answer: the host is down, or on another VLAN
clear the cache for one interface
toolkit.when: the gateway does not answer ping

toolkit.what: Sends ARP requests directly. Works even when ICMP is blocked, and `-D` detects a duplicate IP on the segment.
flags: duplicate address detection: any reply means someone else has the IP

toolkit.what: Watch ARP on the wire with MAC addresses. Shows who asks, who answers, and whether two machines answer for one IP.

toolkit.cmd: ip link add link eth0 name eth0.20 type vlan id 20
toolkit.what: Creates a tagged VLAN subinterface, for a host on a trunk port. Give it an address like any other interface.
toolkit.example: sudo ip link add link eth0 name eth0.20 type vlan id 20 && sudo ip link set eth0.20 up

toolkit.what: On NetworkManager hosts (most desktops, RHEL, Fedora): the address, gateway and DNS that DHCP handed out, and the connection in use.
flags: current IP, gateway, DNS per device
the same view on systemd-networkd hosts

toolkit.what: Link speed, duplex and whether a link is detected. A port negotiated to 100 Mb/s or half duplex explains "the network is slow" on one machine.

steps.prompt: Match each output to what it tells you.
pairs: ARP for the gateway got no answer
the interface is administratively down or unplugged
another machine already uses that IP
DHCP never gave this device an address

steps.prompt: A new server gets an address by DHCP but cannot ping its gateway `10.0.20.1`. `ip neigh` shows `10.0.20.1 dev eth0 INCOMPLETE`. The switch port was meant to be in VLAN 20. What is the most likely cause?
options: The switch port is in the wrong VLAN, so ARP for the gateway never reaches it
steps.explain: ARP is a broadcast on the local segment. If the gateway never answers, the two are not on the same layer-2 network. A gateway that only blocks ICMP still answers ARP, so `ip neigh` would show `REACHABLE`.

steps.prompt: Users report that `10.0.0.50` "comes and goes". `tcpdump -nn -e arp` shows replies for `10.0.0.50` from two different MAC addresses. What is going on?
options: Two machines use the same IP, so the other hosts' ARP caches flip between them
The DHCP lease is too long
steps.explain: Classic duplicate address. Find both MACs (the first half names the vendor), fix the static address or DHCP reservation, and use `arping -D` before assigning static IPs.

steps.prompt: Create a tagged interface for VLAN 30 on the trunk `eth1`.
steps.code: sudo ip link add __1__ eth1 name eth1.30 type __2__ id 30
steps.explain: `link eth1` names the parent interface and `type vlan id 30` adds the 802.1Q tag.

steps.prompt: A host on the LAN cannot reach its gateway. Check from the bottom layer up.
lines: ip -br link   # is the interface UP with a carrier?
ip -br a   # did it get the right address and prefix?
ip neigh show 10.0.0.1   # does ARP for the gateway resolve?

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: When a machine cannot reach anything, start at the link (`ip -br link`, `ethtool`) and the ARP cache (`ip neigh`) before you look at routes or DNS. `INCOMPLETE` or `FAILED` for the gateway almost always means the wrong VLAN, the wrong subnet or a dead link.
